pk.context: 0.6 mg oral, steady state, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is about 45%, and food changes the extent of absorption by only about 15%. Protein binding is low, at 39%, and 40% to 65% of an oral dose is recovered unchanged in urine.
clues.substance: An alkaloid of molecular weight 399.4, occurring as a powder that is soluble in water.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as a single tablet strength.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Not to be given with P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors when renal or hepatic impairment is present; diarrhea and pharyngolaryngeal pain are common.
clues.indication: Prophylaxis and treatment of gout flares in adults, and familial Mediterranean fever in adults and children four years or older.
clues.mechanism: Inhibits beta-tubulin polymerization into microtubules, which prevents neutrophil activation, degranulation and migration.

tell: Its tubulin-binding mechanism and fatal interaction risk with P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors set it apart.

evidence.pk.halfLifeH: the mean elimination half-lives in young healthy volunteers (mean age 25 to 28 years of age) is 26.6 to 31.2 hours
